steps.label: create the dpdbg singleton
steps.expect: zero exit, id 0. The verb takes no arguments: restool hardcodes the root container and pins dpdbg_id=0, which also means the non-root half of DPDBG-I1 is restool-unreachable — a raw-command probe for a later change, recorded as such, not silently dropped. Runs after the driven vdpdbg1 trace has destroyed its object, so this is a fresh create for the probe half

steps.label: second create refused (singleton half of DPDBG-I1)
steps.expect: firmware should refuse a second dpdbg — capture the exact MC status the error path prints (DPDBG-I1 is board-pending on status codes)

steps.label: enable the MC console
steps.expect: zero exit and nothing else observable — SET has no GET (DPDBG-I2). restool's set takes exactly one module option per invocation (rev-1 finding: an if/else-if chain rejects combined options), so the three visibility knobs are three steps. Residue is cleared by V-DPRTC-3's closing reboot

steps.label: enable log printing
steps.expect: zero exit, write-only like every set

steps.label: raise the logging level for dump visibility
steps.expect: zero exit; must precede the dumps — their output goes to the MC log gated by exactly these knobs (dpdbg.md silent-failure trap)

steps.label: out-of-range set level
steps.expect: dpdbg.md unknown 2: rejected or silently clamped? restool does no range validation, so 99 reaches firmware — capture exit and stderr; a clamp is unobservable by design, which is itself the finding

steps.label: dump memory
steps.expect: exit status proves nothing (DPDBG-I3): the artifact is an MC-log line, visible only if the MC console is reachable. Record the exit shape; check the MC console if one is attached, otherwise note the artifact as unobserved

steps.label: dump an unhandled object type
steps.expect: dpdbg.md unknown 1: does DPDBG_DUMP of a type the firmware does not handle return a nonzero MC status, or 0 with only an MC-log line? Capture the exit shape either way

steps.label: destroy the probe dpdbg
steps.expect: the verb takes no object argument (id pinned to 0) and prints 'is destroyed' unconditionally even on its error branch — the read-back is the only trustworthy face

steps.label: root container census after the probe half
steps.expect: zero exit; back at the boot population — no dpdbg, no scratch container residue
